Let \(X=\cos x,\ Y=\cos y\), and set
\[
L=-\Delta-1,\qquad u=AX+BY+w,\qquad w\perp \operatorname{span}\{X,Y\}.
\]
The complement equation is
\[
Lw=Q\{\delta u+\eta u^2-u^3\}.
\]
Using
\[
\cos mx\cos nx=\frac12(\cos(m+n)x+\cos|m-n|x),
\]
and \(L(\cos mx\cos ny)=(m^2+n^2-1)\cos mx\cos ny\), the finite weighted expansion through the needed order gives, after substituting \(\eta^2=9/22\),
\[
P\{\delta u+\eta u^2-u^3\}_X
=
A\left[
\delta-\frac{12}{11}(A^2+B^2)
+\delta\left(\frac{19}{44}A^2+\frac{27}{22}B^2\right)
-\frac34A^4-\frac{465}{242}A^2B^2-\frac{465}{484}B^4
\right],
\]
and symmetrically for the \(Y\)-equation. Since the displayed system is the negative of this projected residual,
\[
p=\frac{19}{44},\quad q=\frac{27}{22},\quad r=\frac34,\quad s=\frac{465}{242},\quad t=\frac{465}{484}.
\]

The potential is
\[
V=-\frac{\delta}{2}(A^2+B^2)+\frac{3}{11}(A^2+B^2)^2
-\delta\left[\frac p4(A^4+B^4)+\frac q2A^2B^2\right]
+\frac r6(A^6+B^6)+\frac s4(A^4B^2+A^2B^4).
\]
Writing \(A=\rho\cos\theta,\ B=\rho\sin\theta\), with \(z=\cos^2\theta\sin^2\theta\), and minimizing in \(\rho\), the leading value is \(\rho^2=\frac{11}{12}\delta+O(\delta^2)\). Hence
\[
V_{\min}(\theta)
=-\frac{11}{48}\delta^2
+\delta^3\left(
\frac{77}{13824}-\frac{583}{2304}z
\right)+O(\delta^4).
\]
Thus
\[
C_0=\frac{77}{13824},\qquad C_1=-\frac{583}{2304}.
\]
Since \(C_1<0\), the energy is minimized when \(z\) is maximal, i.e. \(|A|=|B|\). The higher-order reduction selects the diagonal directions.

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{19}{44},\frac{27}{22},\frac34,\frac{465}{242},\frac{465}{484},\frac{77}{13824},-\frac{583}{2304}\right)}
\]
